candidates.headline: Cache-relative renumbering conflicts with preserving original token distances across evicted spans.

candidates.mechanism: Benchmark constants such as query cadence and answer lag are design choices; claiming they reflect real-world chat requires validation against a distribution of real interactions. The 10-line/20-line setup encodes an assumption that questions pertain to recent information; the paper does not show this lag distribution is representative.

candidates.headline: Stable streaming perplexity does not imply long-term memory or retrieval from evicted tokens.
candidates.claim: Stable streaming perplexity and recent-context QA accuracy under StreamingLLM do not guarantee long-term memory or retrieval of evicted middle tokens.
candidates.paper_fact: While StreamingLLM improves the efficiency of LLMs in streaming contexts, it does not extend the models’ context window or enhance their long-term memory capabilities.
candidates.premise: A KV cache that keeps only initial sink tokens and a recent window cannot attend to evicted middle tokens; retrieval from those tokens requires their KV or equivalent memory.
candidates.inference: A model can show stable next-token PPL and good recent-context QA while failing a query whose answer was evicted, because the evicted KV is unavailable to attention.
candidates.toy_example: Toy example (not a measurement): a unique code is placed at token 10, then 10k tokens later the stream asks for it with a 1k cache; the code is evicted, so stable next-token PPL does not predict recall.
candidates.conditional_consequence: If a task requires an answer from tokens outside the sink+recent cache and no external memory/context extension is used, then stable PPL does not predict task success; StreamEval-style accuracy can fall to zero beyond cache distance.
candidates.critical_link: The evicted tokens are absent from the attention denominator/numerator, so the model cannot retrieve them; stable PPL measures local next-token prediction, not long-range recall.
necessary_conditions: Task requires information from tokens evicted from the sink+recent cache
No external retrieval, context extension, or recomputation supplies the evicted content
Evaluation query-answer distance exceeds retained cache span
defeaters: Answer is in recent window or sink tokens
Task only needs short-term/local context
External memory or context-extension method is combined with StreamingLLM
Cache is large enough to retain the needed span
do_not_infer: Do not infer StreamingLLM is unstable for all streaming tasks
Do not infer perplexity is uninformative for local language modeling
Do not infer the paper claims long-term memory capability
author_boundaries: Paper explicitly limits StreamingLLM to short-term memory and recent context; it does not claim long-term memory.
Paper reports StreamEval accuracy drops beyond cache capacity; it does not claim retrieval from evicted tokens.
inferred_consequences: Stable PPL/QA on recent context can coexist with zero accuracy on queries whose answers were evicted.
StreamingLLM should not be used for long-document QA/summarization without external memory or context extension.

quotes.quote: While StreamingLLM improves the efficiency of LLMs in streaming contexts, it does not extend the models’ context window or enhance their long-term memory capabilities.
Consequently, StreamingLLM is not suitable for tasks that demand long-term memory and extensive data dependency, such as long document question-answering (QA) and summarization.
However, accuracy diminishes as this distance increases and eventually drops to zero when it surpasses the cache capacity.

candidates.headline: Constant memory does not imply or guarantee stable long-text modeling.
candidates.claim: Window attention's constant memory and decoding speed after cache fill are efficiency properties, not evidence of stable long-text language modeling; the paper reports perplexity collapse once sequence length exceeds cache size.
candidates.paper_fact: Although it ensures constant memory usage and decoding speed after the cache is initially filled, the model collapses once the sequence length exceeds the cache size
candidates.premise: A memory bound limits resource use; it does not by itself establish output quality or stability.
candidates.inference: Therefore, evaluating window attention only by constant memory would miss the reported quality failure beyond cache size.
candidates.toy_example: Not a measurement: a 4-token window on a 10-token stream evicts token 0 at step 5; if token 0 is a sink, PPL can jump even though only one old token was removed.
candidates.conditional_consequence: If deployment requires stable long-stream quality, then constant-memory window attention is insufficient unless sink retention or recomputation is added.
candidates.critical_link: The reported PPL spike occurs exactly when cache overflow evicts initial tokens, linking the efficiency mechanism to a quality failure.
necessary_conditions: sequence length exceeds cache size
initial tokens are evicted
quality is measured by PPL or accuracy on long streams
defeaters: task only needs recent context within cache
sink tokens are retained
cache size covers the whole sequence
do_not_infer: Do not infer window attention is never useful.
Do not infer constant memory causes collapse.
Do not infer all eviction policies fail.
Authors do not claim StreamingLLM extends context window.
